name: analysis_status
description:
Check whether IDA's auto-analysis has work outstanding. Non-blocking.

On a freshly opened binary, analysis runs in the background and the function
list, xrefs, strings and decompiler output are all INCOMPLETE until it
settles. Check this before drawing conclusions from a first pass, and use
analysis_wait() to drive it to completion.

`queue_empty` is a SNAPSHOT, not a latch. It reports IDA's auto_is_ok() at
this instant — "are the analysis queues empty right now". IDA re-queues work
as it goes, so the value can read True and then False again moments later;
observed live on a 23MB DLL. Read it as:

  queue_empty=False -> definitely still working, do not trust results yet
  queue_empty=True  -> nothing queued at this instant; combine with a stable
                       function_count across calls before treating analysis
                       as done

`finished` is kept as an alias of `queue_empty` for compatibility and
carries the same caveat.

name: analysis_step
description:
Drive IDA's auto-analysis queue for a bounded slice, then return.

Prefer analysis_wait(), which calls this in a loop with a real timeout.

IDA's background analysis stalls short of completion: measured on a 23MB
DLL it climbed to 73,928 functions on its own and then sat there, never
flipping auto_is_ok(). Something has to drain the residual queue.

Stepping one address at a time keeps each call bounded by max_sec, so the
instance stays responsive through the long bulk phase. Once the range is
drained this makes one closing auto_wait() call, which is unbounded and is
the only thing that actually flips auto_is_ok() — see the comment below.
That final slice therefore runs past max_sec.

max_sec.description: Seconds to spend driving analysis (default 5, max 30)

name: analyze_batch
description:
Analyze multiple functions in one call. Selectively include decompilation,
disassembly, xrefs, strings, and callees per function. More efficient than
calling analyze_function N times — single IDA round-trip.

name: analyze_component
description:
Analyze related functions as a group: per-function compact summaries,
internal call graph (edges only between supplied functions), shared globals,
interface vs internal classification, and strings used by multiple members.

name: analyze_function
description:
Compact single-function analysis: pseudocode (capped at 100 lines), top
strings, top non-trivial constants, callers, callees, xrefs, comments, and
basic block summary. Use this for "tell me everything about function X" in
one call instead of chaining decompile + callees + xrefs_to separately.

include_asm.description: Include full disassembly (default: false, saves tokens)

name: append_comments
description:
Append comments at addresses, deduping exact text by default. Unlike
set_comments (which overwrites), this preserves existing annotations — use
it for incremental commentary. scope='auto' (default) writes a function
comment when addr is a function start, otherwise a line comment; force
with scope='func' or 'line'. dedupe=True skips writes when the exact
stripped text already appears on its own line.

dedupe.description: Skip if exact text already exists (default: true)
Skip if exact text already exists (default: true)

name: basic_blocks
description: Get control flow graph basic blocks for functions

addrs.description: Function addresses to get basic blocks for

max_blocks.description: Max basic blocks per function (default: 1000, max: 10000)

name: binary_fingerprint
description:
Content fingerprint of the loaded binary for similarity index keying.

Returns the input file's sha256 and md5 (hex, or null if unavailable), the
total function count, and an arch label (e.g. 'x86_64'). The sha256 keys the
per-binary similarity index so the same binary shares one index across
instances; md5 is the fallback when sha256 is unavailable.

name: callees
description: Get functions called by the specified functions

addrs.description: Function addresses to get callees for

name: callgraph
description: Build call graph starting from root functions

roots.description: Root function addresses to start call graph traversal from

max_depth.description: Maximum depth for call graph traversal

max_nodes.description: Max nodes across the graph (default: 1000, max: 100000)

max_edges.description: Max edges across the graph (default: 5000, max: 200000)

name: classify_functions
description:
Classify functions as thunk/wrapper/leaf/dispatcher/complex based on
size, callee count, and flags. Use '*' (default) for all non-library
functions. Returns paginated results sorted by address.

addrs.description: Function addresses (or '*' for all non-library functions)

name: declare_stack
description: Create stack vars

name: declare_type
description:
Declare C types (structs, unions, enums, typedefs) into the IDB.

Takes ordinary C declaration text. Declare a type here first, then apply it
to an address with set_type.

name: decompile
description:
Decompile one function to Hex-Rays pseudocode.

The single most useful tool for understanding behaviour. Requires the
Hex-Rays decompiler. For many functions at once use decompile_to_file —
decompiling in a loop blocks the instance for every other caller.

name: define_code
description:
Convert raw bytes to a code instruction at each given address. Returns
{addr, ea, length} on success (length is the instruction byte length) or
{addr, ea, error} if create_insn failed. Use this when IDA classified an
instruction as data or failed to decode.

end.description: Optional end address for explicit bounds
Optional end address for explicit bounds

name: define_func
description:
Define a function at each given address. IDA infers bounds unless an
explicit end address is provided. Returns {addr, start, end} on success or
{addr, start, error} if the function already exists or add_func fails.
Use this when IDA auto-analysis missed a function entry point.

end.description: Optional end address for explicit bounds
Optional end address for explicit bounds

name: delete_stack
description: Delete stack vars

name: diff_before_after
description:
Apply a rename/type/comment action and return the before/after decompilation
side by side. Actions: 'rename_func' ({name}), 'set_type' ({type}),
'set_comment' ({comment}). Useful to verify a rename or type change actually
improved readability. Returns {before, after, action_applied, changes_detected}.

name: disasm
description: Disassemble function to assembly instructions

name: enum_upsert
description:
Create or extend local enums in an idempotent way. Creates the enum if
it doesn't exist, then upserts each member: skips if name+value already match,
reports conflict if name or value collides with a different entry. Never
destructively replaces existing members.

queries.description: Enum upsert: name, members [{name, value}], bitfield (optional bool)

name: export_funcs
description:
Export function data (addresses, names, sizes, prototypes) in bulk.

Prefer this over looping a per-function tool — one call instead of N round
trips against a single-threaded IDA instance.

format.description: Export format: json (default), c_header, or prototypes

name: find
description: Search for patterns in the binary (strings, immediate values, or references)

name: find_bytes
description: Search for byte patterns in the binary (supports wildcards with ??)

name: find_regex
description: Search strings with case-insensitive regex patterns

pattern.description: Regex pattern to search for in strings

name: find_xref_signatures
description:
Find signatures for code locations that reference an address. For each
input address, finds all code cross-references TO it, generates a unique
signature at each xref site, and returns the shortest ones. Ideal for
creating signatures for data addresses, vtable entries, or string
references that can't be signatured directly.

addrs.description: Address(es) or name(s) to find XREF signatures for (e.g. a data address referenced by code)

top.description: Number of shortest signatures to return per address (default: 5)

name: func_features
description:
Extract name-independent similarity features for functions, page by page.

Per function returns: size, is_named, CFG metrics (bb/edge/complexity/loops/
callee/caller counts + out-degree sequence), a 64-perm instruction-shingle
MinHash, external API (import) callees, referenced strings, non-trivial
immediate constants, and — only for named functions — pseudocode identifier
tokens. Feed pages into the server-side similarity indexer. Use '*' to iterate
all functions; only the page slice is analyzed so large binaries stay bounded.

addrs.description: Function addresses (comma-separated or list), or '*' for all

name: func_profile
description:
Per-function profile: size, basic block count, cyclomatic complexity,
callee/caller counts, and string count. Useful for prioritizing which
functions to analyze deeply. Fills the gap between list_funcs (too little
info) and analyze_function (too expensive per call).

sort_by.description: Sort key: size, complexity, xref_count, callee_count, name (default: size)

name: func_query

queries.description: Function query: filter, name_regex, min_size, max_size, has_type, sort_by, descending, offset, count

name: func_tokens
description:
Emit jTrans-style normalized instruction token streams per function, for a
neural BCSD embedding backend. Uses IDA's own operand normalization (registers
kept, stack vars -> var_xxx/arg_xxx, imm/disp -> CONST, intra-function jumps ->
JUMP_ADDR_<idx>) -- which a byte/objdump reproduction cannot match. Paginated
like func_features; returns ``{addr: [token, ...]}``.

addrs.description: Function addresses (comma-separated or list), or '*' for all

name: get_bytes
description:
Read raw bytes at one or more addresses.

Reads the static IDB image, not a live process. Uninitialised BSS reads
back as zeroes rather than 0xFF.

addr.description: Address to read from (hex or decimal)
Address to read from (hex or decimal)

name: get_global_value
description:
Read global variable values by address or name
(auto-detects hex addresses vs names)

queries.description: Global variable addresses or names to read values from

name: get_int
description: Read integer values from memory addresses

addr.description: Address to read from (hex or decimal)
Address to read from (hex or decimal)

queries.description: Integer read requests (ty, addr). ty: i8/u64/i16le/i16be/etc

name: get_string
description:
Read NUL-terminated strings at one or more addresses.

Use when you have a pointer from decompiler output; to search for a string
by content use find(type="string") instead.

name: idb_save
description:
Save active IDB to disk, with no dialogs. Call after renaming, retyping,
or commenting to persist changes. Optionally specify a custom output path
to write a copy instead, leaving the open database untouched.

path.description: Optional destination path (default: current IDB path)

name: imports
description:
List imported functions grouped by source module.

Useful early: the import set is a fast signal of what a binary can do
(networking, crypto, process injection) before you decompile anything.

name: imports_query
description:
Query imports with module and name filters. Example:
{module: 'kernel32', filter: '*File*'} to find all kernel32 file I/O imports.

queries.description: Import query: filter (import name pattern), module (module name pattern), offset, count

name: infer_types
description:
Infer the type of data or a function at an address.

Asks Hex-Rays first and falls back to IDA's own guess. Returns the inferred
type plus a confidence label; a null type means neither could decide.

name: insn_query

queries.description: Instruction pattern: mnem, op0, op1, op2, op_any, func, segment, offset, count

name: int_convert
description:
Convert numbers between hex, decimal, binary and ASCII, in batch.

Pure computation — no IDB access, so it needs no instance state.

size.description: Byte size for conversion (omit for auto)
Byte size for conversion (omit for auto)

inputs.description: Convert numbers to various formats (hex, decimal, binary, ascii)

name: list_funcs
description:
List functions in the binary, paginated.

Requires auto-analysis to be finished — call analysis_wait() first on a
freshly opened binary or this returns a partial list. On large binaries use
count/offset rather than fetching everything; count=0 with a glob filter is
a full scan.

filter.description: Optional glob pattern to filter results

count.description: Maximum number of results (default: 50, 0 for all)

filter.description: Optional glob pattern to filter results

count.description: Maximum number of results (default: 50, 0 for all)

queries.description: List functions with optional filtering and pagination

name: list_globals
description:
List global variables (non-function named addresses), paginated.

Requires auto-analysis to be finished — call analysis_wait() first on a
freshly opened binary or names will still be missing.

filter.description: Optional glob pattern to filter results

count.description: Maximum number of results (default: 50, 0 for all)

filter.description: Optional glob pattern to filter results

count.description: Maximum number of results (default: 50, 0 for all)

queries.description: List global variables with optional filtering and pagination

name: lookup_funcs
description:
Resolve functions by address or by name; the form is auto-detected.

Accepts 0x-prefixed addresses, sub_XXXX names, or real symbol names. Use
this to turn a name from decompiler output into an address to work with.

name: make_signature
description:
Create unique byte signatures for addresses. Generates the shortest
unique signature starting at each address by walking instructions and
wildcarding operands. Useful for finding stable patterns that survive
recompilation.

addrs.description: Address(es) or name(s) to create unique signatures for (e.g. '0x401000', 'main', or ['0x401000', 'sub_402000'])

wildcard_operands.description: Wildcard instruction operands for relocatable signatures (default: true)

max_length.description: Maximum signature length in bytes before giving up (default: 1000)

name: make_signature_for_function
description:
Create unique byte signatures for function entry points. Resolves each
name/address to a function, then generates the shortest unique signature
starting at the function start.

addrs.description: Function address(es) or name(s) to create signatures for (e.g. 'main', '0x401000', or ['main', 'sub_402000'])

wildcard_operands.description: Wildcard instruction operands for relocatable signatures (default: true)

max_length.description: Maximum signature length in bytes before giving up (default: 1000)

name: make_signature_for_range
description:
Create a byte signature for a specific address range (e.g. a selected
region). Unlike make_signature, this does NOT guarantee uniqueness — it
simply encodes the bytes in the range with optional operand wildcarding.

wildcard_operands.description: Wildcard instruction operands for relocatable signatures (default: true)

name: patch
description: Patch bytes at memory addresses with hex data

name: patch_asm
description: Patch assembly instructions at addresses

name: put_int
description: Write integer values to memory addresses

addr.description: Address to write to (hex or decimal)

value.description: Integer value as string (decimal or 0x..; negatives allowed for signed)

addr.description: Address to write to (hex or decimal)

value.description: Integer value as string (decimal or 0x..; negatives allowed for signed)

items.description: Integer write requests (ty, addr, value). value is a string; supports 0x.. and negatives

name: py_eval
description:
Execute Python code in IDA context.
Returns dict with result/stdout/stderr.
Has access to all IDA API modules.
Supports Jupyter-style evaluation.

name: read_struct
description:
Reads struct type definition and parses actual memory values at the
given address as instances of that struct type.

If struct name is not provided, attempts to auto-detect from address.
Auto-detection only works if IDA already has type information applied
at that address

Returns struct layout with actual memory values for each field.

name: refresh_caches
description: Force-refresh all caches (strings, functions, globals).

name: rename
description: Unified rename operation for functions, globals, locals, and stack variables

func_addr.description: Function address containing the local variable
Function address containing the local variable
Function address containing the stack variable
Function address containing the stack variable

name: search_structs
description:
Find structures whose name contains a substring (case-insensitive).

Returns name, size and field count. Use read_struct to see the fields or to
overlay the struct on an address.

filter.description: Case-insensitive substring to search for in structure names

name: server_health
description:
Health/ready probe for MCP server and current IDB state. Returns
uptime, IDB path, auto-analysis status, Hex-Rays availability, and
strings cache state.

name: server_warmup
description:
Warm up IDA subsystems to reduce first-call latency. Call after
connecting to a new instance to ensure analysis is complete and caches
are populated before running tools.

name: set_comments
description: Set comments at addresses (both disassembly and decompiler views)

name: set_type
description: Apply types (function/global/local/stack)

name: stack_frame
description:
List the stack frame variables of one or more functions.

Returns each local's name, offset, size and type — the frame layout behind
the var_NN names in decompiler output.

name: struct_member_upsert
description:
Upsert struct members by offset (gap-fill, retype, rename) idempotently.

Fills a reverse-engineered struct in incrementally without rewriting the
whole declaration. Existing members never shift. Replacing a *named* member
requires old_type as a guard so concurrent work is not silently clobbered;
gaps need no guard. Use dry_run to validate a batch first.

offset.description: Byte offset of the member within the struct (hex or int)

old_type.description: Type or member name that must currently cover the offset. Required when the target is a named member (guards against clobbering work); optional when the target is a gap.

size.description: Integer member size: 1/2/4/8 -> uint8/16/32/64 (use size OR type)

type.description: C type name or declaration for the new member (use size OR type)

offset.description: Byte offset of the member within the struct (hex or int)

old_type.description: Type or member name that must currently cover the offset. Required when the target is a named member (guards against clobbering work); optional when the target is a gap.

size.description: Integer member size: 1/2/4/8 -> uint8/16/32/64 (use size OR type)

type.description: C type name or declaration for the new member (use size OR type)

dry_run.description: Validate only (check offsets/old_type/new type); no changes

offset.description: Byte offset of the member within the struct (hex or int)

old_type.description: Type or member name that must currently cover the offset. Required when the target is a named member (guards against clobbering work); optional when the target is a gap.

size.description: Integer member size: 1/2/4/8 -> uint8/16/32/64 (use size OR type)

type.description: C type name or declaration for the new member (use size OR type)

offset.description: Byte offset of the member within the struct (hex or int)

old_type.description: Type or member name that must currently cover the offset. Required when the target is a named member (guards against clobbering work); optional when the target is a gap.

size.description: Integer member size: 1/2/4/8 -> uint8/16/32/64 (use size OR type)

type.description: C type name or declaration for the new member (use size OR type)

dry_run.description: Validate only (check offsets/old_type/new type); no changes

queries.description: Replace gap/placeholder or named struct members by offset without shifting layout

name: survey_binary
description:
Get a compact overview of the binary in one call. Returns file metadata,
segment layout, entry points, statistics, top 15 strings and functions ranked
by xref count (functions include classification: thunk/wrapper/leaf/dispatcher/
complex), imports by category, and call graph summary. Use this as your FIRST
tool call when starting analysis. Do not call list_funcs, imports, or find_regex
separately for triage — this returns all of that. Use detail_level='minimal'
for binaries with >10k functions.

name: trace_data_flow
description:
Follow cross-references from or to an address, automatically traversing
multiple hops. 'forward' follows xrefs-from, 'backward' follows xrefs-to.
Returns nodes (with function name, instruction, code/data classification) and
edges. Do not use for call graph traversal — use callgraph for that.

name: ui_dialogs
description:
Inspect or clear a modal dialog that blocks IDA (GUI only).

IDA runs no tool while a modal dialog is open, so other tools fail with
'IDA is blocked by a modal dialog'. Call this with action='list' to see
which dialog it is. Only dismiss or accept a dialog that your own call
opened, or when the user asked you to; a dialog the user opened may hold
their unsaved input. Message boxes raised by a tool are already
auto-dismissed, and listed under recently_dismissed.

action.description: list|dismiss|accept|unstick. list (default): report the open modal dialog, if any. dismiss: close it as if Escape/Cancel was pressed. accept: press its default button. unstick: clear a stuck cancellation flag and a leaked batch mode.

name: undefine
description:
Undefine item(s) at each address, converting them back to raw bytes.
Size is determined from `end` (exclusive) or `size`; defaults to 1 byte.
Uses ida_bytes.DELIT_EXPAND so adjacent items spanning into the range are
fully removed. Returns {addr, start, size} on success.

name: xref_query
description:
Query cross-references with direction and type filters.
direction='to' finds refs TO addr, 'from' finds refs FROM addr, 'both' finds all.
type_filter='code' shows only code xrefs, 'data' only data, 'all' shows both.
Supports dedup and pagination.

queries.description: Xref query: addr, direction (to/from/both), type_filter (code/data/all), offset, count

name: xrefs_from
description:
Get cross-references from specified addresses (symmetric with xrefs_to).
Returns outgoing code and data references for each address.

name: xrefs_to
description: Get cross-references to specified addresses

name: xrefs_to_field
description: Get cross-references to structure fields
